contract.title: Pressure drop, water at 20C, 5mm parallel-plate gap, length solved for exactly 10 Pa, Ubar=0.02 m/s
contract.requested_prompt: Show that the pressure drop in a 2D water channel (height 5 mm, 0.02 m/s) is exactly 10 Pa.
contract.reference: Fully-developed plane-Poiseuille pressure drop: dp = 12*mu*L*Ubar/H^2 (White, Viscous Fluid Flow). Hydrodynamic entrance length and excess pressure-drop correction K_inf~=0.6 for parallel plates: Shah, R.K. & London, A.L. (1978), Laminar Flow Forced Convection in Ducts, Academic Press.

objectives.description: Solver completes normally on the frozen, budget-compliant case with no numerical faults.
Mesh is orthogonal and low-skew, supporting the assumption that discretization error is small relative to the comparison tolerance (no independent grid-convergence sweep was run).
Volumetric flux balances across inlet/outlet/walls at the final state.
Flow has reached a statistically steady state over the final 37.5 s (25%) window.
Achieved mean inlet velocity reproduces the requested 0.02 m/s and the outlet pressure BC is applied as specified.

CFD inlet-to-outlet pressure drop agrees with the analytic plane-Poiseuille value (the channel length was solved from this relation to target exactly 10 Pa) within a tolerance that accounts for entrance-region development over the finite solved length.

checks.rationale: Solver must exit normally having reached the registered horizon; a crashed or truncated run cannot support any downstream claim.
No FOAM FATAL ERROR / segfault / sigFPE signature may appear in the solver log.

A fixed, exactly-representable deltaT=2^-4=0.0625s (power-of-two binary fraction; a prior investigation of this same class of case found non-power-of-two deltaT crashed from floating-point Time accumulation) keeps Co well under 1 on this mesh/velocity combination; an upper bound of 1.0 confirms the fixed time step kept the Courant number subcritical throughout, including the startup transient.
checkMesh must report Mesh OK with no serious errors.
Executed mesh must have exactly the planned 12000 cells (300x40x1), confirming the budget-constrained (<50000 cell) mesh was built as specified.
checkMesh must report exactly 2 non-empty solution directions, confirming the case is genuinely 2-D as required.
Executed case files must hash-match the frozen case; no post-freeze edits are permitted.
p and U must be finite (no NaN/Inf) in every saved state.

A structured rectangular hex mesh should be exactly orthogonal (0 deg); an upper bound of 5 deg screens for a blockMeshDict topology error and supports treating discretization error as small for the Poiseuille comparison.
Low skewness on the orthogonal grid is required for the linear/central discretization schemes used to remain close to their nominal truncation error.
Inlet+outlet+wall volumetric flux must sum to ~0 at the final state for an incompressible flow; 1% allows for the finite GAMG pressure-equation tolerance.
No-slip walls must pass zero net volumetric flux; any nonzero value reflects floating point round-off only.
The run must actually cover the registered 37.5 s stationarity window before any steadiness claim can be evaluated.
Inlet/outlet net-flux mismatch over the final 37.5 s (25% of the horizon) must stay small, confirming volumetric steady state.
Per-step inlet/outlet flux and domain monitors must show <2% relative span over the stationarity window.
Volume-weighted relative L2 change of p and U between the start and end of the stationarity window must be small, confirming the fields themselves (not just integrated fluxes) have settled.
The run must reach the registered 150.0 s target time; otherwise this is a development run, not a finished result.

The inlet patch volumetric flux (phi, outward-normal convention so inflow is negative) must equal -Ubar*H*D = -1.000e-07 m^3/s to within 1%, confirming the fixedValue inlet velocity BC (0.02 m/s mean) was applied and resolved as specified; this is expected to be nearly exact since it follows directly from a Dirichlet boundary condition, not from flow development.

The outlet p boundary condition is fixedValue uniform 0 (kinematic gauge pressure reference); the domain-wide minimum of p should sit at this value to within a small numerical band (3% of the expected kinematic pressure drop), confirming the gauge-pressure reference was applied as intended and that p does not undershoot below its physically expected range.

The channel length L=1.0396 m was solved from dp=12*mu*L*Ubar/H^2 to make the fully-developed (infinite-plate) analytic prediction exactly dp_analytic=10.0000 Pa at the stated H=0.005 m, Ubar=0.02 m/s and documented-default water properties. The measured hydrodynamic entrance length Le~=0.06*Re_Dh*Dh~=0.1195 m (Re_Dh=199.2) is ~11.5% of the 1.040 m channel, so this finite-length channel's true inlet-to-outlet pressure drop is expected to exceed the idealized infinite-plate value by the Shah & London asymptotic entrance-excess correction K_inf*0.5*rho*Ubar^2=0.1198 Pa (~1.2% of dp_analytic), giving a pre-registered best-estimate total of dp_total_expected=10.1198 Pa. The check is centered on this combined best estimate (not the idealized value alone, which would ignore a known, named physical effect) with a symmetric 5% band covering <=2% expected mesh/iterative discretization error plus residual uncertainty in the Shah & London correlation, without being loose enough to mask a genuine solver defect. This band fully contains the user-requested 10 Pa target, which differs from the best estimate only by the pre-registered, physically-named entrance effect.

assumptions.justification: Explicitly stated in the request ("water channel").
Not stated by the user; 20 C / 1 atm is the standard engineering reference condition for "water" properties.
Standard density of water at 20 C, 1 atm from NIST/engineering reference tables.
Standard dynamic viscosity of water at 20 C, 1 atm from NIST/engineering reference tables.
nu = mu/rho using the documented-default water properties above.
Explicitly stated in the request ("height 5 mm").
Explicitly stated in the request ("0.02 m/s").

NOT stated by the user. Pressure drop depends on length via dp=12*mu*L*Ubar/H^2, so an 'exactly 10 Pa' target under-determines the geometry unless L is fixed. In the absence of the user, L is derived analytically (not fitted post-hoc) by solving the fully-developed plane-Poiseuille relation for the L that gives dp_analytic=10 Pa exactly at the stated H, Ubar, and documented-default water properties. This is the only self-consistent way to honor all of 'height 5 mm', '0.02 m/s', and 'exactly 10 Pa' simultaneously; a user should confirm whether a specific channel length was intended instead.

The request gives only a mean velocity with no upstream conditioning detail; a flat/uniform inlet profile is the standard engineering default and lets the flow develop naturally over the finite solved length, which is the physically relevant scenario for the requested pressure drop.
Re_H = Ubar*H/nu = 99.62 (Re_Dh = 199.2 on a hydraulic-diameter basis), well below transition (~2300), confirming laminar flow is physically appropriate.

limitations: Channel length was derived, not user-specified; a different intended length would give a different true pressure drop under otherwise-identical physics.

The 5% pressure-drop tolerance embeds an a-priori engineering entrance-effect estimate (Shah & London K_inf~=0.6); it is not independently isolated from this single CFD run (would require a second, much longer channel to separate entrance from fully-developed pressure drop).
Water properties are fixed at 20 C/1 atm with a constant-nu Newtonian model; no temperature dependence, compressibility, or non-Newtonian effects are modeled.

A flat/uniform inlet velocity profile was assumed in the absence of upstream conditioning information in the request; an already-parabolic inlet profile would reduce the entrance-effect bias discussed in the pressure-drop check.
Single-mesh verification; no independent grid-convergence (GCI) sweep was run, so discretization error is bounded only by the orthogonality/skewness screen, not directly measured.
